fig:measured.caption: \textbf{A trajectory-derived reading is compared with a situation-conditioned human range, with explicit abstention.} \textbf{a} A causal trajectory window supplies the IPV reading; the current observable situation supplies its human reference range. Readability and human support are checked before a verdict is issued. Outside-range directions are more assertive (A) and more accommodating (C); W is within range. Objective outcomes and subjective ratings evaluate departures and do not enter the monitor. \textbf{b} One illustrative interaction, with ego and counterpart trajectories and time markers. The conflict-zone circle is a schematic locator, not a measured road boundary. \textbf{c} Its frame-level reading and frozen $90\%$ reference, with a verdict strip. Grey intervals and gaps denote abstention, never a zero reading or a within-range verdict. No curve is interpolated across those gaps. The example is descriptive and contains within-range and accommodating verdicts. Estimator mechanics and reference-population summaries appear in Supplementary Fig.~\ref{fig:suppcandidate} and Extended Data Fig.~\ref{fig:eddistribution}. Source Data accompany this figure.

fig:context.caption: \textbf{Human interaction is relational and context-dependent.} \textbf{a} Joint distribution of event-level partner IPV summaries for $34{,}850$ independent valid cases. Each case is displayed in both partner orders; this symmetry does not double $n$. \textbf{b} Exchangeable intraclass correlations (ICCs) and matched re-pairing references, by source and pooled. Source estimates use 34,850 cases in total, while the matched-support pooled analysis includes $34{,}757$ cases; its correlation is $-0.338$ versus $+0.041$ after re-pairing. The independent implementation uses 34,645 cases and has no supplied interval. \textbf{c} Existing out-of-fold AUC trajectories for predicting which partner has the higher late-interaction IPV, defined from the final quarter. This label is not observed passage order. \textbf{d} Paired turning-minus-straight IPV differences, pooled and by source, retaining the source whose interval includes zero. The pooled difference is $+0.079$ [$+0.063,+0.095$]\,rad across $3{,}565$ pairs. \textbf{e} Priority-minus-non-priority differences across three realised post-encroachment-time (PET) bands. PET is an offline descriptive stratification, never an online input. \textbf{f} Merge/pass and same-direction geometry contrasts by source. Intervals are the existing $95\%$ source intervals: case bootstrap for source correlations, scene-cluster bootstrap for the pooled ICC and AUC, central matched-reshuffling intervals for the null, paired-difference $t$ intervals for turning contrasts, case bootstrap for PET strata, and two-group bootstrap for geometry. Cross-source prediction and reference coverage are retained in Extended Data Fig.~\ref{fig:edtransfer}. Source Data specify each panel's population and interval definition.

fig:monitor.caption: \textbf{Conditioning sharpens the human reference at near-nominal coverage, while the gates delimit its use.} \textbf{a} Global and situation-conditioned interval widths at nominal $80\%$, $90\%$ and $95\%$ coverage, expressed as a percentage of the seven-candidate span $3\pi/4\approx2.36$\,rad. Reductions of $21\%$, $20\%$ and $8\%$ are calculated from unrounded widths; the conditional $90\%$ width averages $1.87$\,rad. \textbf{b} Empirical coverage minus nominal coverage in percentage points, with zero marking nominal coverage. Both panels use the same $461{,}937$ accepted moments and describe marginal coverage, not a guarantee for each situation. \textbf{c} Nested natural-driving test-fold counts: $663{,}282$ candidate moments, $486{,}660$ readable, and $461{,}937$ also supported by the human reference; $417{,}036$ are within the $90\%$ range and $44{,}901$ outside. Human-support abstention is $24{,}723/486{,}660=5.08\%$ of readable moments. Failing either gate returns no verdict. \textbf{d} The situation explains $20.9\%$ of reading variance across all $486{,}660$ readable moments, using $1-\mathrm{SSE}/\mathrm{SST}$ for the conditional median against the test-fold mean. The remainder is unexplained by this predictor and is not assigned a psychological interpretation. Source Data accompany this figure.

fig:consequence.caption: \textbf{Assertive-side departures accompany tighter routine interactions without a detected increase in the tested emergency tails.} A denotes the assertive side, C the accommodating side and W within range. \textbf{a} Cumulative distributions of minimum ego-to-counterpart time-to-collision over the frozen three-second post-verdict window, omitting non-closing frames; the full observed range is shown on a logarithmic axis. The assertive upper quartile is $39.9\%$ lower [$16.9,56.4$], while the lower quartile is not compressed and the median contrast remains unresolved. \textbf{b} A--W and C--W share differences for all four nested ego-margin thresholds, in percentage points. \textbf{c} Counterpart speed-reduction and speed-range median ratios relative to W, for both directions. Existing ratio intervals are retained because corresponding accommodating-side absolute-difference intervals are unavailable; absolute differences are not inferred from them. \textbf{d} Both direction-specific share differences for all three nested counterpart-braking thresholds, using acceleration records. Panels \textbf{a},\textbf{b} use 499 A, 817 C and 12,344 W moments across 227 scenario runs. Counterpart data use 469 A, 719 C and 10,483 W anchors across 175 runs; \textbf{d} pools 13,800, 21,025 and 310,246 acceleration records, respectively. Intervals are pointwise $95\%$ whole-run bootstrap intervals: 2,000 draws for quantile and speed ratios and 1,000 for threshold differences. Moments and records are not independent resampling units. Full steering and threshold results remain in Source Data. All associations are descriptive.

fig:humanarm.caption: \textbf{The same human reference audits matched human drivers and automated systems; their larger rate difference is accommodating.} \textbf{a} Outside-range rates under the frozen $90\%$ reference: the natural-driving test population, matched human arm and matched automated arm. The natural rate is an alarm-inflation check, not a same-condition comparison. The human rate has the existing driver-by-scenario bootstrap $95\%$ interval of $3.4$--$5.5\%$; the dashed line marks the nominal $10\%$ outside rate. The matched AV/human ratio is $1.95$ [$1.62,2.39$], from the existing scenario bootstrap. \textbf{b} Direction-specific point estimates: assertive AV $519/14{,}099=3.68\%$ and human $435/15{,}598=2.79\%$; accommodating AV $869/14{,}099=6.16\%$ and human $351/15{,}598=2.25\%$. Both denominators are judgeable moments in the corresponding arm; side-specific intervals are unavailable. \textbf{c} The 15 paired scenario flag rates with equal axes and the equality line, retaining all observed scenarios as point estimates. \textbf{d} The common assertive-to-within consequence signature, separating routine margins, counterpart response and emergency tails. Filled markers denote AVs and open markers humans. Existing ratio intervals are shown where available; daggers mark unavailable ratio intervals, including both human margin estimates and the emergency-tail ratios. Missing intervals do not establish precision or non-detection. Other nominal coverage levels are retained in Supplementary Fig.~\ref{fig:supphumanlevels}. Source Data document each endpoint's denominator and interval.

fig:subjective.caption: \textbf{Subjective ratings distinguish perceived atypicality from comfort and reported interaction cost.} \textbf{a} Perceived atypicality ($8-\mathrm{Q1}$), \textbf{b} comfort (Q4), and \textbf{c} reported counterpart interaction cost (Q5), for supplied assertive-side (A), accommodating-side (C) and within-range comparison (W) segments. Ego and counterpart positions are distinguished by marker shape and fill; Q5 is counterpart-only and structural ego blanks are not zeroes. Each position contributes 158 A, 239 C and 199 W ratings, from 40 participants in 20 pairs. Class means average repeated ratings within participant and then weight participants equally. Bars are existing pointwise $95\%$ intervals from 10,000 participant-pair bootstrap draws, conditional on selected stimuli. Direct within-participant contrasts are displayed separately; significance is not inferred from overlap of class-mean intervals. The full 30-comparison family uses Holm correction (Supplementary Tables~\ref{tab:subjective_core} and~\ref{tab:subjective_full}); ego A--W atypicality has adjusted $p=0.0704$, and A--C non-detection does not imply equivalence. Scenario-composition sensitivity is shown in Supplementary Fig.~\ref{fig:suppsubjectivesensitivity}. Segment labels do not specify every frame's verdict, and W may include abstention. Source Data contain aggregate results only.
